text:
Maggie L: Quick sync — thinking about simplifying the automatic fallback policy panel. Current UX shows too many knobs. Can we agree on a reduced set for the first pass?
Raj S: +1. Which knobs are you thinking to keep?
Maggie L: Proposal: keep three visible controls — (1) degrade mode (Graceful | Failover | Throttle), (2) trigger source (Error-rate | Latency | Quota), (3) audit retention window (30d/90d/365d). Advanced options hidden behind 'show advanced'.
Carmen: That seems reasonable. Question: do we expose token-budget as a trigger in the main view? Customers mention token-based throttles often.
Elena (PM): Token budget is important but I worry about cognitive overload. Maybe primary trigger list should be metric categories, and token-budget can be a prefilled advanced trigger with a tooltip.
Maggie L: Yeah — keep it advanced. For degrade modes I think labels should be user-friendly: Graceful -> "Reduced fidelity", Failover -> "Switch model variant", Throttle -> "Limit requests".
Raj S: UX nit: show a one-line preview of what each mode does inline. Eg: "Reduced fidelity — prefer cached responses and lower sampling."
Tess (Product Ops): Need to capture who changed policies for audit. We should mandate a short change-reason on every save (required field) and attach user id + timestamp to the audit event.
Maggie L: Agree. Also thinking about a playback link on the audit entry — click -> run simulation for the last 24h of traffic showing how many requests would have hit fallback. Useful for validation.
Carmen: Simulation is great but heavy. We can provide a quick estimate (count + percent) and a deeper playback job that runs async with a link/email when ready.
Raj S: Implementation detail: the decision trace must include the matched trigger comparator and the matched threshold value so we can reenact exactly. Eg: {"trigger":"p95_latency","window":"5m","threshold_ms":1200}.
Maggie L: Good point — include trigger payload in audit. Also store resolved model variant mapping for failover so playback uses same fallback.
Elena (PM): On the UI side, small clarifying copy: "When enabled, Auto-fallback will route requests to a fallback model or reduce fidelity based on configured triggers. Auditable actions are logged and can be replayed." Keep it short.
Tess (Product Ops): How long should audit records be retained by default? 90d seems a decent default; enterprise can request 365d.
Carmen: Default 90d + a checkbox to opt into longer retention for enterprise tenants. Also need export button (CSV/ndjson) for forensic teams.
Maggie L: Permissions: only users with role 'policy-admin' can edit; viewers can see the audit and trigger history. Make that explicit in the panel header.
Raj S: Edge case: if a fallback is triggered across multiple regions, playback should indicate per-region counts and allow filtering.
Maggie L: Yep — add region filter and a small note: "Playback is approximate when cross-region caches are enabled."
infra-bot: deploy-notice: staging rollout for "autofallback-panel-v1" scheduled at 2029-11-12T03:00Z.
Elena (PM): Can we add a quick-policy-sanity check on save? Eg: warn if you set failover to a smaller model with significantly different tokenizer or lower context window.
Raj S: We can run a lint step comparing model capabilities and show a yellow warning if potential regression. Not block save, just warn and require acknowledgement.
Tess (Product Ops): Add a required acknowledgement when auto-fallback uses models without matching safety filters. Must be explicit.
Maggie L: UX mock next: I'll drop a prototype in Figma with compact layout + hover tooltips. Who wants to review Monday?
Carmen: I'll take the first pass on the simulation UX.
Raj S: I can spec the audit payload and the decision trace schema.
Elena (PM): I'll own copy and the required change-reason flow.
Tess (Product Ops): I'll draft the retention + export policy and the RBAC mapping.
Maggie L: Great — let's reconvene Tue after the mocks. Thanks all :thumbsup:
